subject.title: Slug alias quota (25) blocking legitimate naming migration — publisher nitishgargiitd

question: Should ClawHub grant this verified publisher a one-time, account-scoped historical-slug exception, or require selected legacy redirects to be released first?
rationale: The quota protects a namespace and redirect-reservation boundary, so choosing an exception, a redirect-release policy, or a broader quota change requires human authorization rather than an automated code repair.

options.title: Grant a scoped migration exception
options.body: After verifying publisher control and the 13 listed mappings, temporarily raise or bypass the quota only for this migration and retain an audit record.

options.title: Release selected aliases first
options.body: Ask the publisher to identify low-value legacy redirects that may be safely relinquished before completing the remaining renames.

options.title: Revisit the general quota policy
options.body: Open a separate product/security discussion only if similar verified migrations show that the fixed cap is systematically inadequate.

recommendation.title: Grant a scoped migration exception
recommendation.body: After verifying publisher control and the 13 listed mappings, temporarily raise or bypass the quota only for this migration and retain an audit record.

likelyOwner.reason: Most likely available decision owner for the repository-level namespace and authorization policy; direct quota-code ownership remains unconfirmed.
